items.markingKey: ½ mark each: streptokinase – enzyme produced using microbes; lipases – enzyme produced using microbes; beer – beverage made without distillation; pectinases – enzyme produced using microbes.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilisers is incorrect?
items.answer: Ladybirds are used to control mosquitoes.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Ladybirds are used to control mosquitoes.” Correct form: Ladybirds control aphids; dragonflies control mosquitoes.
options: Ladybirds are used to control mosquitoes.
Trichoderma species are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens.
Bt toxin is released in the gut of the larvae and kills them.
Baculoviruses are species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticides.

items.stem: What is meant by “sewage”?
items.answer: The municipal waste-water generated every day in cities and towns, containing large amounts of organic matter and microbes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the municipal waste-water generated every day in cities and towns, containing large amounts of organic matter and microbes.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an enzyme produced using microbes?
items.answer: beer
items.markingKey: (d) Beer is a beverage made without distillation, not an enzyme produced using microbes.
options: streptokinase
proteases
lipases
beer

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Citric acid is produced by Acetobacter aceti.”
items.answer: Citric acid comes from Aspergillus niger; Acetobacter aceti makes acetic acid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Citric acid comes from Aspergillus niger; Acetobacter aceti makes acetic acid.

items.stem: At a sewage treatment plant near Nagpur, Harleen finds that the BOD of the primary effluent is 200 mg L⁻¹ and that of the water leaving the aeration tank is 50 mg L⁻¹. Calculate the percentage reduction in BOD. What does this reduction indicate?
items.answer: 75% reduction; most organic matter has been consumed by microbes
items.markingKey: Reduction = (200 − 50)/200 × 100 = 75% (1); BOD measures the oxygen needed by microbes to oxidise organic matter, so a lower BOD means less organic matter / pollution potential (1).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Baculoviruses are desirable in IPM programmes.
Reason (R): They are species-specific and do not harm non-target insects.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Protects beneficial insects.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about microbes in sewage treatment and biogas production is correct?
items.answer: The greater the BOD of waste water, the greater is its polluting potential.
items.markingKey: (c) The greater the BOD of waste water, the greater is its polluting potential. The other statements are false. High BOD indicates high organic matter and polluting potential. Biogas is predominantly methane, with CO₂ and H₂. They use anaerobic bacteria that digest bacteria and fungi in the sludge, producing biogas.
options: Anaerobic sludge digesters use aerobic bacteria.
Low BOD indicates highly polluted water.
The greater the BOD of waste water, the greater is its polluting potential.
Biogas is mainly carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Which term describes an enzyme such as streptokinase used to remove clots from blood vessels?
items.answer: a clot buster
items.markingKey: (a) A clot buster: an enzyme such as streptokinase used to remove clots from blood vessels.
options: a clot buster
antibiotics
distillation
a starter (inoculum)

items.stem:
A stage of sewage treatment has these features: anaerobic bacteria act; methane, H₂S and CO₂ formed; bacteria and fungi in sludge are digested.
(i) Which stage is it? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were primary treatment? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Anaerobic sludge digestion (ii) part of activated sludge pumped into digesters (iii) filtration and sedimentation; grit (soil and pebbles) removed
items.markingKey: (i) anaerobic sludge digestion – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: part of activated sludge pumped into digesters – 1 mark. (iii) for primary treatment: physical removal of particles; filtration and sedimentation; grit (soil and pebbles) removed – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: A stage of sewage treatment has these features: physical removal of particles; primary sludge settles; grit (soil and pebbles) removed. Which stage is it? Give a reason.
items.answer: Primary treatment
items.markingKey: 1 mark: primary treatment; 1 mark: the features physical removal of particles; primary sludge settles; grit (soil and pebbles) removed are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which product is obtained from Aspergillus niger?
items.answer: citric acid
items.markingKey: (b) Aspergillus niger gives citric acid: organic acid producer.
options: statins
citric acid
acetic acid
curd

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of sewage treatment: filtration and sedimentation (primary), effluent released into water bodies, aeration with flocs (secondary). Give a reason.
items.answer: filtration and sedimentation (primary) → aeration with flocs (secondary) → effluent released into water bodies
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order filtration and sedimentation (primary) → aeration with flocs (secondary) → effluent released into water bodies; 1 mark for the reason: Primary physical treatment, then biological treatment and sludge digestion.

items.stem: What is the role of Azotobacter as a biofertiliser?
items.answer: free-living nitrogen fixation in soil
items.markingKey: (b) Azotobacter: free-living nitrogen fixation in soil.
options: nitrogen fixation in paddy fields and adding organic matter
free-living nitrogen fixation in soil
symbiotic nitrogen fixation in root nodules of leguminous plants
absorption of phosphorus from soil

items.stem: Which of the following statements about microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilisers is correct?
items.answer: Bt toxin is released in the gut of the larvae and kills them.
items.markingKey: (c) Bt toxin is released in the gut of the larvae and kills them. The other statements are false. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in root nodules of legumes; Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living. They are species-specific and narrow-spectrum with no negative impact on non-target organisms. They kill both useful and harmful organisms indiscriminately.
options: Baculoviruses are broad-spectrum insecticides that also kill beneficial insects.
Rhizobium fixes nitrogen as a free-living bacterium in soil.
Bt toxin is released in the gut of the larvae and kills them.
Chemical pesticides kill only harmful insects.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Explain the term “distillation”.
items.answer: The process used to produce hard liquors such as whisky, brandy and rum from fermented broth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the process used to produce hard liquors such as whisky, brandy and rum from fermented broth.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between primary treatment and anaerobic sludge digestion on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A stage of sewage treatment has these features: primary sludge settles. Which stage is it – primary treatment or anaerobic sludge digestion? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Primary treatment: physical removal of particles; filtration and sedimentation; grit (soil and pebbles) removed. Anaerobic sludge digestion: part of activated sludge pumped into digesters; anaerobic bacteria act; bacteria and fungi in sludge are digested. (b) Primary treatment.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: primary treatment; 1 mark: “primary sludge settles” is a feature of primary treatment.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as beverage made with distillation or enzyme produced using microbes: pectinases, lipases, proteases, whisky.
items.answer: pectinases – enzyme produced using microbes; lipases – enzyme produced using microbes; proteases – enzyme produced using microbes; whisky – beverage made with distillation.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: pectinases – enzyme produced using microbes; lipases – enzyme produced using microbes; proteases – enzyme produced using microbes; whisky – beverage made with distillation.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilisers is incorrect?
items.answer: Chemical pesticides kill only harmful insects.

items.stem: Define the term “activated sludge”.
items.answer: The sediment of bacterial flocs in the settling tank, part of which is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the sediment of bacterial flocs in the settling tank, part of which is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum.
